snp4.5:1.2:
a person makes them
the utmost thing in the world,
snp4.5:1.3:
&, from that, calls
all others inferior
snp4.5:1.4: and so he’s not gone beyond disputes.
snp4.5:2.1: When he sees his own advantage
snp4.5:2.2:
in what’s seen, heard, sensed,
or in habits & practices,
snp4.5:2.4:
he sees all else, all others,
as inferior.
snp4.5:3.1:
That, too, say the skilled,
is a binding knot:
snp4.5:3.2:
that
in dependence on which
you regard another
as inferior.
snp4.5:3.3: So a monk shouldn’t be dependent
snp4.5:3.4:
on what’s seen, heard, or sensed,
or on habits & practices;
snp4.5:4.1: nor should he theorize a view in the world
snp4.5:4.2:
in connection with knowledge
or habits & practices;
snp4.5:4.4:
shouldn’t think himself
inferior or superlative.
snp4.5:5.1:
Abandoning what he’d embraced,
not clinging,
snp4.5:5.2:
he doesn’t make himself dependent
even in connection with knowledge;
snp4.5:5.3:
doesn’t follow a faction
among those who are split;
snp4.5:5.4:
doesn’t fall back
on any view whatsoever.
snp4.5:6.1:
One who isn’t inclined
toward either side
snp4.5:6.4: when considering what’s grasped among doctrines,
snp4.5:7.2:
theorized perception
with regard to what’s seen, heard, or sensed.
By whom, with what,
should he be pigeonholed
here in the world?
snp4.5:8.2:
don’t yearn,
don’t adhere even to doctrines.
snp4.5:8.3:
A brahman not led
by habits or practices,
snp4.5:8.4:
gone to the beyond
—Such—
doesn’t fall back.
